stories.headline: Swedish voters leave election in tight deadlock between political blocs
stories.body:
Swedish voters cast ballots in a closely fought election that could bring the far-right into government [c16].

Sweden is a Nordic nation [c12]. The country has a population of 10.6 million people [c12].

Public broadcaster SVT said the two main political blocs were separated by only 20,000 votes [c1]. This gap was recorded with 50% of the votes counted [c1].

Projected results from Sweden's election authority gave Magdalena Andersson's left-wing bloc a one-seat majority [c2]. Her Social Democrat-led group led over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's coalition [c2].

At 9:45pm local time, SVT projected the opposition bloc leading by 175 seats to 174 seats [c7].

Christian Democrats leader Ebba Busch said the election result may remain uncertain until Wednesday [c10]. Swedish Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard also said results might not be clear until Wednesday [c13]. She explained that election officials are waiting for overseas votes to arrive [c13].

Under Prime Minister Kristersson, Sweden made several major policy changes [c14]. Sweden abolished permanent residency for refugees [c14]. The government also tightened welfare rules [c14]. In addition, authorities increased expulsions [c14].

Kristersson promised cabinet jobs to the hard-right Sweden Democrats if he remains in office [c3]. The Sweden Democrats were founded by Nazi sympathisers in the 1980s [c6].

Partial election results suggest the Sweden Democrats lost support for the first time since 2010 [c4]. The party first entered parliament in 2010 [c4]. Party leader Jimmie Åkesson acknowledged his party lost percentage points compared to 2022 [c9]. He said the party likely lost its status as Sweden's second-largest party [c9]. While voting in the suburb of Rinkeby, Åkesson remarked that it "doesn't look like Sweden" [c15].

Andersson questioned voters about the future of the nation [c5]. She asked if Sweden should have a government entirely dominated by the Sweden Democrats [c5]. She said such a outcome has never happened in Sweden before [c5]. She asked if voters wanted a government led by her instead [c5]. She said her government would steer Sweden in a new spirit of co-operation [c5].

Projected vote shares showed the Social Democrats leading with 27.6% [c8]. The Moderates followed with 20.0% [c8]. The Sweden Democrats received 17.5% [c8]. The Left Party won 8.2% [c8]. The Centre Party reached 7.1% [c8]. The Christian Democrats achieved 6.3% [c8]. The Green Party received 6.2% [c8]. The Liberals got 5.5% [c8].

Liberal Party leader Simona Mohamsson called her party's election results a historic comeback [c11].

vocab.meaning: a group of political parties joining together to form a government
the acts of forcing people to leave a country

stories.headline: Six dead and over 100 missing after ferry capsizes in Indonesia's Java Sea
stories.body:
Rescue teams searched for over 100 missing people after a ferry capsized in Indonesia's Java Sea [c17, c18, c22].

The passenger ferry Virgo Transport 8 carried 213 passengers and 30 crew members [c19]. France 24 reported that the ferry carried 243 people between Java and Borneo [c22]. Six people died and 107 were rescued [c17]. But France 24 reported at least one person died [c22]. At least 130 people were reported missing after contact was lost during bad weather [c18]. France 24 reported more than 100 people remained missing [c22].

The vessel departed Surabaya at 10:33 on Saturday [c20]. It was scheduled to reach Banjarmasin at 14:00 on Sunday [c20]. The Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office received a report two hours after losing contact at about 2am Sunday [c29].

Indonesian Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said helicopter surveillance confirmed the ferry capsized but had not sunk by 3pm [c23]. Search and rescue chief I Putu Sudayana said rescue ships fought waves up to 2.5 metres high [c24].

The 119-metre ferry was built in Japan in 1987 [c26]. It was operated by PT Virgo Karya Shipping [c26]. The ship was carrying 89 vehicles [c27].

Government data shows 111 ship accidents were recorded in Indonesia between 2020 and 2026 [c21]. Four days earlier, a ferry fire in the Philippines killed at least 76 people [c28].

vocab.meaning: close observation of an area from above or afar

stories.headline: Russian drone strikes Ukrainian passenger train near Polish border
stories.body:
Russian forces launched a jet-propelled drone that struck a Ukrainian passenger train running between Kyiv and Warsaw near the Polish border [c30, c34].

The drone hit the locomotive at Yahodyn after an evacuation order was given 15 minutes earlier [c34]. The strike occurred two kilometres from the border [c30].

Former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson was at the Yagodyn station nearby around the time of the attack [c31]. Former CIA Director David Petraeus was also at the station [c31]. Railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said a diplomatic train carrying Johnson departed early due to timetable changes [c35]. Former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt said passengers on his train prepared for evacuation before arriving safely in Poland [c37].

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the strike was terror knocking at the doors of the EU and Nato [c36]. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that he expects Russia to escalate the war [c38]. Russia's Defence Ministry said strikes targeted railway infrastructure transporting European military cargo [c39].

Overnight Russian attacks using over 450 drones and missiles killed at least six people across Ukraine [c43]. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 405 drones and four missiles [c43].

vocab.meaning: a powered rail vehicle used for pulling a train
stopped or caught something before it reached its destination

stories.headline: Oil prices surge following military strikes on Saudi Arabia and Gulf shipping
stories.body:
Houthi militants attacked Saudi oil pipelines and ships in the Gulf, driving up global energy prices [c44, c54].

Brent crude futures rose $3.62 to $108.23 per barrel after the strikes [c44]. WTI crude futures rose $3.15 to $103.20 per barrel [c45].

An attack on an Iranian cargo ship off Qeshm Island killed one person and wounded four others [c47]. The UKMTO reported a severe fire on a vessel hit by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz [c48]. About one-fifth of world oil and LNG passed through the strait before war broke out on February 28 [c49].

Scheduled negotiations in Oman between Iran and Gulf Arab states were postponed [c46]. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi announced on X that the meeting was postponed for consensus [c51]. Iranian state media said the postponement was a joint decision requested by regional countries [c52].

Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Saudi Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud in New Delhi [c53]. They discussed militant attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline [c54]. Iraq said recent attacks on the pipeline were launched from Iraqi territory [c55].

vocab.meaning: financial contracts to buy or sell commodities at a set price in the future
an object fired or launched as a weapon

stories.headline: United States defeats France to win 12th Women's Basketball World Cup
stories.body:
The United States basketball team defeated France 97-79 in Berlin to win the Women's Basketball World Cup [c56].

The win gave the US team its 12th World Cup title [c56]. France led the US by two points at halftime [c57]. France opened a 14-point lead early in the second quarter after a 21-2 run [c64]. But the US outscored France 30-12 in the third quarter [c57].

Breanna Stewart scored a game-high 22 points for the US [c58]. Jackie Young scored 18 points [c58]. Caitlin Clark scored 12 points in the final after scoring one point in the semifinal [c59]. For France, Gabby Williams scored 16 points in the first half and four in the second half [c60].

France earned silver in its first World Cup final appearance [c63]. The US extended its unbeaten run at the Olympics and World Cups to 20 years [c62]. The team secured its fifth consecutive World Cup title [c62]. The US has not lost a World Cup match since 2006, extending its streak to 36 wins [c65].

Spain won bronze by defeating Germany 81-58 [c61]. Point guard Iyana Martin scored 20 points for Spain [c66].

vocab.meaning: following continuously in an unbroken order
a continuous series of successes or events

stories.headline: World leaders gather in New Delhi for BRICS summit on global reforms and cooperation
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Chinese President Xi Jinping at the BRICS summit in New Delhi [c67].

The two leaders held discussions on the sidelines of the summit on September 12, 2026 [c67]. Prime Minister Modi spoke to President Xi about their shared border [c70]. He said peace in border areas remains an essential basis for bilateral relations [c70]. He added that tranquility in those areas is necessary for the continued development of ties [c70].

BRICS member nations signed a major document called the New Delhi Declaration 2026 [c68]. The declaration called for reforms to the UN Security Council [c68]. It also called for greater participation of developing economies in global decision-making [c68].

China and Russia again stated support for two key member nations [c69]. They backed the aspirations of Brazil and India to play a greater role in the United Nations [c69]. This support includes a larger role on the UN Security Council [c69].

During the final session of the summit, Prime Minister Modi raised warnings about global risks [c73]. He warned world leaders against the weaponisation of technology [c73]. He also warned against the weaponisation of critical minerals [c73].

India served as the host nation for the summit under four foundational pillars [c74]. The four pillars of India's BRICS chairship were resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability [c74].

Prime Minister Modi also held a meeting with Philippines President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on September 13, 2026 [c71]. The two leaders agreed to expand bilateral cooperation across key sectors [c71]. They agreed to work together more closely in defence [c71]. They agreed to expand security cooperation [c71]. They also agreed to deepen ties in trade and space [c71].

In addition, Prime Minister Modi held bilateral meetings on the margins of the summit with several African and Asian leaders [c72]. He met with the leader of South Africa [c72]. He spoke with the leader of Kazakhstan [c72]. He held discussions with the leader of Uganda [c72]. He met with the leader of Nigeria [c72]. He also held talks with the leader of Burundi [c72].

vocab.meaning: a formal explicit statement or announcement

stories.headline: Indian crew member missing after oil tanker attack off Oman coast
stories.body:
India condemned an attack on a Panama-flagged oil tanker off the coast of Oman [c75].

The attack targeted the MT El Gaia on September 13, 2026 [c75]. Thirteen Indian crew members of the ship were rescued [c76]. Search and rescue operations continued for one missing Indian seafarer [c76].

During the BRICS summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed a Seafarers' Emergency Support Network [c77]. The proposal aims to safeguard mariners working in conflict zones [c77].

Indian seafarers account for over 12% of the global merchant shipping workforce [c81]. They comprise nearly 312,000 of the world's 2.57 million seafarers [c81]. Ten Indian seafarers are among 16 Indians killed in the West Asia conflict [c78]. Another five Indian seafarers have died in strikes on merchant vessels in the Black Sea [c78].

In a separate event, an Iranian cargo vessel was struck near Qeshm Island on September 13, 2026 [c79]. The strike in the Strait of Hormuz left one person dead and four injured [c79]. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said the strait would open if the United States terminates its blockade [c80].

vocab.meaning: a person who travels or works at sea
the closing off of a port or region by military forces

stories.headline: India wins Women's Asia Cup but declines trophy from tournament chief
stories.body:
The Indian women's cricket team defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in Dubai to win the Women's Asia Cup [c82].

The victory on September 13, 2026, marked a record-extending eighth title for the team [c82, c86]. Shafali Verma scored 68 runs off 39 balls [c88]. Smriti Mandhana scored 59 runs off 39 balls [c88]. Together they built a 129-run opening partnership for India [c88]. Indian bowler Shree Charani took four wickets for 20 runs [c89]. Sri Lanka were bowled out for 111 [c89].

The Indian team refused to collect the trophy from Asian Cricket Council President Mohsin Naqvi [c83]. Naqvi is also Pakistan's interior minister [c83]. Indian head coach Amol Muzumdar said the decision was made by the Board of Control for Cricket in India [c84].

The Indian men's cricket team similarly declined to receive the Asia Cup trophy from Naqvi in September 2025 [c85]. Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu accepted the runners-up cheque from Naqvi during the presentation ceremony [c87].

vocab.meaning: a formal ceremony where awards or prizes are handed out
a period of batting together by two players in cricket
